newsitem.title: UK: Eurobourses rally, lira up on ERM membership.
newsitem.headline: Eurobourses rally, lira up on ERM membership.

text.p: European bourses traded bullishly on Monday on the back of yet another record closing high on Wall Street and the lira, buoyed by re-entry into Europe's Exchange Rate Mechanism (ERM), strengthened against the mark.

London, Europe's biggest stock exchange, shot up 32 points or 0.8 percent in early trade before slipping back slightly. It extended a late Friday surge sparked by optimism over Tuesday's budget, a fresh outbreak of bid speculation and the latest record peak on Wall Street, which saw an almost two percent rise over the course of last week.
On the foreign exchanges, the lira rallied in immediate reaction to the announcement late on Sunday that it had re-joined the European exchange rate mechanism (ERM) at a 990 per-mark mid-point.
Italy had been ejected from the ERM in 1992 by a wall of foreign exchange bets against the lira.

Early on it firmed to within a whisker of its new central rate at 990.15 per mark, from around 999 late in Europe, before slipping a little in late morning to around 993.7. "I think a lot of the good news has been priced in for the lira, so I would be surprised if there was much more large-scale buying of lira," said a trader at a Swiss Bank.
The dollar was buoyant against the mark and just below session peaks against the yen at midday in Europe and dealers said it was riding on the back of lira developments.
"The lira is strengthening. Money is flowing out of the Deutsche mark and this is having an effect on the dollar," said Elizabeth Legge, London-based economist at Bankgesellschaft Berlin.

In equities, traders said the London bourse was focused on the budget, hoping for a fiscally tight package that would ease pressure on interest rates to cool the pace of growth. They saw the FTSE pushing towards its intraday record of 4,073.2 set on October 21.
On Friday the blue chip index broke through 4,000 for the first time in November to close up 64.9 points, its biggest one-day gain in 16 months.

Analysts warned, however, that a statement due Monday afternoon by Chancellor Kenneth Clarke on the government's position on European monetary union could upset the market by rekindling political uncertainties ahead of an election which must be held by next May.

In Frankfurt German shares also opened floor trading well up and looked set to penetrate the 2,800 watershed on the DAX index. At 1130 GMT the DAX was up 25.5 at 2788.89 - just ten points below its record trading peak set on November 15.
Deutsche Telekom, floated last week in the largest share sale in European history, was again the heaviest-traded stock.
On the Paris bourse, French shares traded on a higher note following their near-one percent gain on Friday.

Analysts said the underlying tone remained positive although some viewed the market as ready for a consolidation after recent gains. Fire-hit Eurotunnel, however, shed 10 percent after weekend press reports that its re-opening for passenger traffic would miss the lucrative Christmas period, with only freight being allowed through the link for months to come
Meanwhile, on the bullion market, gold fell and made its lowest fixing since March 1995 at $375.10 per ounce.
"We are at new lows for the year and if it falls beyond $375, it could get very ugly," one dealer said.
Gold has been under pressure recently from selling by producers and continung talk of central banks considering making sales of metal from their bullion reserves.
CURRENCIES AT 1130 GMT
The dollar was quoted at 112.56 yen and 1.5135 marks against 111.34 yen and 1.5039 marks late on Friday.
STOCK MARKETS AT 1130 GMT
The Financial Times-Stock Exchange index of 100 leading British shares was up 24.6 points at 4,043.3.
In Paris, the CAC-40 share index was up 20.04 at 2,275.51.
The 30-share DAX index in Frankfurt was up 25.5 at 2,788.89.
PRECIOUS METALS
Gold fixed at $375.10, down from Friday's close of 377.15. Silver was down five cents at $4.84.
